Regarding the tenth, 'the contemplation of correspondence with the inexhaustible': it is because one contemplates this meaning and its opposite according to reality."

"11. The Contemplation on the Inexhaustibility of the Nature of Wisdom in the Site of Enlightenment" means that one manifests sitting at the site of enlightenment in accordance with the faith of sentient beings.
As the sutra says: "Good son!..."
"This is called the eleven kinds of inexhaustible contemplations of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Having explained how they are realized,
next, for what purpose they are taught, the fifth section— the manifestation of fifty remedial methods— is presented.
The Sūtra says:
Furthermore, son of good family!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of remedial dharmas.
What are the ten? First, it counteracts the mind of stinginess and greed by raining down the rain of giving.
Second, it counteracts the mind of immoral conduct by purifying the three dharmas of body, speech, and mental action.
Third, it counteracts the mind of ill-will by practicing pure great compassion.
Fourth, it counteracts the mind of indolence by seeking all Buddha-dharmas without weariness.
Fifth, it counteracts the mind of unwholesome discursive thought by attaining the mastery of meditative concentration, liberation, and heroic prowess.
Sixth, it counteracts the mind of delusion by generating the skillful means of wisdom that brings about certainty.
Seventh, it counteracts the mind of various afflictions by giving rise to the factors that assist the path.
Eighth, it counteracts the path of perversion by gathering the factors that assist the true truths, thereby giving rise to the non-perverted path.
Ninth is the counteractive to the lack of mastery, because one attains mastery over the Dharma regarding what is timely and untimely.
Tenth is the counteractive to the mark of selfhood, because one contemplates the selflessness of all phenomena.
"Good son! These are called the ten kinds of remedial dharmas of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
The treatise says:
The Sūtra states: "Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of remedial dharmas," because the ten pāramitās are purified. What are these ten?
First is the purity of the *dānapāramitā*, as the sūtra says: "Because it counteracts the mind of stinginess and greed by raining down the rain of giving.
Second is the purity of the *śīlapāramitā*, as the sūtra says: "Because it counteracts the mind of broken precepts through the three purities of the actions of body, speech, and mind."
Third is the purity of the *kṣānti-pāramitā*, as the sūtra states: "Because one practices pure great compassion as an antidote to the mind of malice.
Fourth is the purity of the *vīrya-pāramitā*, as the sūtra states: "Because one seeks all Buddha-dharmas without weariness as an antidote to the mind of indolence."
Fifth is the purity of the dhyāna-pāramitā, as the sūtra states: "Because one counteracts unwholesome vitarka and vicāra, attaining mastery in the dhyānas, liberations, and prātihāryas."
Sixth is the purity of the *prajñāpāramitā*, as the sūtra states: "Because it gives rise to the skillful means of wisdom that assists certainty by counteracting the mind of delusion."

Seventh is the purification of the perfection of skillful means (*upāya-pāramitā*), as the sūtra says: "Because it counteracts the mind of all afflictions and gives rise to the factors that assist the path.

Eighth is the purification of the perfection of aspiration (*praṇidhāna-pāramitā*), as the sūtra says: "Because it counteracts the path of perversion, accumulates the aids to the path of the true truths, and gives rise to the non-perverted path."

Ninth is the purification of the *bala-pāramitā* (perfection of power), as the sūtra states: "Because one attains mastery over the time and non-time of dharmas, counteracting the lack of self-mastery.
Tenth is the purification of the *jñāna-pāramitā* (perfection of wisdom), as the sūtra states: "Because one contemplates the selflessness of all dharmas, counteracting the mark of a self (*ātman*)."
As it is said in the Sūtra: "O son of good family!
These are called the ten kinds of remedial dharmas of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Thus, the purpose for which they were taught has been explained.
Next, it is explained where [the bodhisattva] dwells; the sixth, the ten kinds of stages of tranquility (*śāntabhūmi*), are demonstrated.
The Sūtra says:
"Furthermore, noble son!"
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of peaceful stages (*śāntabhūmi*). What are the ten?
First is the peace of the body, because they are free from the three types of unwholesome bodily karma.
Second is tranquility of speech, because of the purification of the four types of vocal karma.
Third is tranquility of mind, because of being free from the three types of mental misconduct.
Fourth is inner tranquility, because of non-attachment to one's own body.
Fifth is tranquility regarding external objects, because of non-attachment to all phenomena (*dharma*).
Sixth is tranquility regarding the merit of wisdom, because of non-attachment to the path.
Seventh is supreme tranquility, because of observing the noble stages as they truly are.
Eighth is tranquility until the end of the future, because of supporting practice with wisdom that reaches the further shore.
Ninth is the tranquility of worldly activities, because of not deceiving any sentient beings.
Tenth is the tranquility of not cherishing body or mind, because of teaching and transforming all sentient beings with great compassion.
"Good son! These are called the ten stages of tranquility of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
The treatise says:
The Sūtra says: "Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of stages of tranquility (*śānti-bhūmi*). What are the ten?
First is the tranquility of the body, because of being free from the three unwholesome paths of action of the body."
"Second is tranquility of speech, because of the purity of the four types of vocal karma;
third is tranquility of mind, because of being free from the three types of mental misconduct," [this is said] because of the purity of the three types of virtuous precepts.
"Fourth, inner tranquility, because of non-attachment to one's own body," means because of being free from the false view of a self (*ātman*).

"Fifth, tranquility regarding external objects, because of non-attachment to all phenomena (*dharma*)," means because of being free from [the views of] permanence and impermanence regarding phenomena.
"Sixth is the tranquility of the merit of wisdom, because of non-attachment to the path" means because of non-attachment to the existence or non-existence of things.

"Seventh is supreme tranquility, because of observing the noble stages as they truly are" means because one does not perceive the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, but observes the noble stages of the Buddhas and bodhisattvas as they truly are.
"第八，the quiescence of the future limit, because one aids practice with the wisdom of the other shore," means that one is far removed from all false grasping at signs.

"Ninth, the worldly affairs he engages in are quiescent because he does not deceive any sentient beings" means that, by knowing the conventional truth (*saṃvṛti-satya*) and the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*) as they truly are, he teaches the Dharma without error.
"Tenth, the tranquility of not begrudging body or mind" means that for the sake of teaching and transforming all sentient beings, one does not grow weary regardless of where one is born.
As the Sūtra says: "Good son!
These are called the ten stages of tranquility of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Thus has the realization of the dharma-realm been explained.
From this point onward, the meaning of the practice that accords with reality as it is will be explained in succession for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
The Sūtra says:
"Furthermore, son of good family!"
All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attain awakening through practice in accordance with reality, not through practice that does not accord with reality.
Good son, what is meant by "the practice of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in accordance with reality"?
"Good son! One who practices according to reality is so called because they are able to act in accordance with what they have taught.
One who does not practice according to reality is so called because they possess only words and cannot practice in accordance with reality."
Furthermore, good son!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have another two kinds of practice that accords with reality. What are these two?
The first is the path of practicing according to reality through wisdom;
the second is the path of practicing according to reality through abandonment. Good son!
This is called the two kinds of practice according to reality for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, good son,
all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have another two kinds of practice according to reality.
What are these two? First, practicing in accordance with reality by disciplining oneself;
second, practicing in accordance with reality by teaching and transforming sentient beings.
"Good son! These are called the two kinds of practice according to reality for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, good son!"
Furthermore, there are two kinds of practice according to reality for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these two?
First is the practice according to reality through the wisdom of effortful application; [the second is the practice according to reality through effortless spontaneity].
Second is the practice of non-effortful wisdom (*anābhoga-jñāna*) as it truly is.
Son of good family!
These are called the two kinds of practice as it truly is for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, good son!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have another two kinds of practice in accordance with reality. What are these two?
First, skillfully knowing how to distinguish the various stages and practicing according to reality;
second, skillfully knowing the expedient means that are without differentiation among the stages and practicing according to reality. Good son!
This is called the two kinds of practice according to reality for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, son of good family,
there are again two kinds of practice according to reality for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
What are these two? First, practicing in accordance with reality by remaining free from the faults of the various stages;
second, practicing in accordance with reality by skillfully knowing the methods for transitioning from stage to stage.
"Good son! These are called the two kinds of practice according to reality for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, good son!"
Furthermore, there are two kinds of practice according to reality for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
What are these two? The first is the ability to explain the practice according to reality regarding the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
Second, they skillfully know the expedient means for non-retrogression from the Buddha’s bodhi and practice accordingly in accordance with reality.
Good son! These are called the two kinds of practice in accordance with reality of the Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
The Treatise says:
The Sūtra states, "Furthermore, son of good family!
All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attain awakening through practice that accords with reality, not through practice that does not accord with reality."
Good son! What is called the "practice according to reality" of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas?
Practice according to reality means being able to act in accordance with what one has spoken.

Regarding the statement, "Those who do not practice according to reality merely engage in verbal discourse and cannot practice according to reality," this is because they practice exactly as it has been taught, thereby not contradicting their previous words.
Furthermore, the Sūtra says: "Moreover, son of good family!
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have two further kinds of practice in accordance with reality. What are these two?"
The first is the path of practicing according to reality through wisdom;
the second is the path of practicing according to reality through abandonment. Good son!

"This is called the two kinds of practice of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as they truly are" means that while they realize the wisdom of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas through knowing them as they truly are, they do not take that state to be the ultimate goal.
Furthermore, the Sūtra says: "Moreover, son of good family, there are two further kinds of practice according to reality for Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
What are these two?"
"First, 'cultivating oneself through practice in accordance with reality' means practicing in accordance with reality by personally attaining the sublime path.

Second, 'teaching and transforming sentient beings through practice in accordance with reality' means teaching the Dharma in accordance with reality so as to lead other sentient beings to enter the right path."
As the sutra says: "Good son!
These are called the two kinds of practice according to reality for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, the sutra states: "Moreover, good son!"
Furthermore, there are two kinds of practice according to reality for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these two?
First is "practice according to reality through the wisdom of effortful application," which refers to practicing the bodhisattva path by means of the wisdom of effortful mental engagement.

Regarding "second, practicing the wisdom of effortless conduct according to reality": it means that while dwelling in the path of cultivation, the bodhisattva practices the bodhisattva deeds with a mind free from volitional effort, by virtue of the wisdom of effortless conduct.
As it is said in the Sūtra: "Good son, these are called the two kinds of practice according to reality for all Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, the Sūtra says: "Moreover, good son!"
Furthermore, there are two kinds of practice according to reality for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these two?
First, "skillfully knowing and discerning the various stages through practice according to reality," which is due to skillful wisdom and expedient means.

Regarding "second, skillfully knowing the non-differentiation of the stages and practicing according to reality through skillful means," this is because one enters into the single characteristic (*ekalakṣaṇa*).
As the Sūtra says: "Good son!..."
"This is called the two kinds of practice according to reality for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, the sūtra says: "Moreover, son of good family, all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have another two kinds of practice according to reality."
What are these two? First, "practicing according to reality by being free from the faults of the stages" means that one is free from the two extremes.
Second, "practicing according to reality by skillfully knowing the methods for transitioning from stage to stage" means that one practices wholesome dharmas with unremitting diligence.
As the sutra says: "Good son!
These are called the two kinds of practice according to reality for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Furthermore, the sutra states: "Moreover, good son!"
Furthermore, there are two kinds of practice according to reality for bodhisattva-mahāsattvas. What are these two?
The first is being able to explain the practice according to reality regarding the stages of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, because they have skillfully studied all dharmas.

Regarding the phrase, "Second, skillfully knowing the expedient means for non-retrogression from the Buddha's bodhi and practicing accordingly as it truly is": this is because, by realizing *tathatā* (suchness), one knows the expedient means of practice as they truly are.
As the sutra says: "Good son!
These are called the two kinds of cultivation according to reality for all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
The sutra states:
"Good son! Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas possess such immeasurable and boundless practices of reality as these.
All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should train in this way and practice according to reality."
If all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas can practice in this way according to reality, they will swiftly attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi without it being difficult for them.
The Treatise says:
By practicing the four kinds of superior causes, one accomplishes the four kinds of superior fruits and others, because of practicing in accordance with reality.
As for those superior fruits, they consist of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas, which knows the events of the three periods of time within a single thought-moment, as everything is in accord.
The Sūtra says:
At that time, the Buddha praised the Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
Mañjuśrī! You have now skillfully expounded for all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas the path of their original karma.
It is exactly as you have said.
The Treatise says:
"Excellent" is said because he teaches the Dharma without error and because he accords with the Dharma taught by the Tathāgata.
The Sūtra says:
When this Dharma was being taught, ten thousand bodhisattvas attained the patience regarding the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).

Mañjuśrī, the Prince of the Dharma, and all those in the world—gods, humans, asuras, and others—hearing what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The treatise says:
There are three meanings for which one rejoices.
What are these three?
First, the purity of the speaker, because they have attained mastery over all phenomena;
second, the purity of the Dharma taught, because they have realized the pure essence of phenomena as they truly are;
third, the purity of the attainment of the fruit based on the Dharma taught, because they have attained the pure and sublime realm.
As it is said in the sutra: "All were greatly rejoiced, and they believed, accepted, and practiced accordingly.
